title: Gauge Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo Method for Many-Fermion Systems
abstract: We propose novel Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) methods for interacting many-fermion systems by leveraging the stochastic gauge freedom, originally developed in Gaussian phase-space QMC, within the phaseless auxiliary-field QMC (AFQMC) framework. In particular, we reinterpret the conventional force bias in phaseless AFQMC as a drift gauge and explore Fermi gauges based on natural orbitals of a reduced one-body density matrix defined via a mixed estimator, yielding stochastic, time-dependent Hartree-Fock-like dynamics. We propose a symmetry-projection sampling scheme to enhance the sampling efficiency. As a proof of concept, we apply these gauge-augmented AFQMC methods to a simple shell-model Hamiltonian: the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick model. Numerical results illustrate the potential of stochastic gauges to enhance accuracy and reduce fluctuations, underscoring the promise for advancing these new techniques toward more realistic shell-model applications.
summary: This paper advances Quantum Monte Carlo simulations for strongly correlated fermions by introducing gauge augmentation into the AFQMC framework. It reinterprets stochastic process non-uniqueness as a tunable 'gauge' parameter, allowing researchers to dynamically improve sampling efficiency and accuracy. The results demonstrate that these gauge-enhanced methods provide robust tools for tackling complex many-body Hamiltonians.
main_problem: Calculating the ground state properties of interacting many-fermion systems is computationally challenging due to strong correlations and basis set limitations.
main_result: The proposed gauge-augmented AFQMC methods successfully enhance sampling efficiency and reduce statistical fluctuations compared to conventional approaches when applied to models like LMG.
method: The core method involves extending Phaseless Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) by incorporating stochastic gauge freedom, treating the force bias as a drift gauge or utilizing Fermi gauges derived from natural orbitals.
model_or_system: The work focuses on general interacting many-fermion systems, using the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick model as a proof of concept. The underlying physics is described by a second-quantized Hamiltonian with strong correlations.
key_observables: Ground state energy expectation values and systematic bias/statistical fluctuations relative to exact results (FCI).
important_parameters: Interaction strength ($\lambda$), imaginary time evolution parameter ($	au$), and the choice of gauge parameters ($g_s$).
main_assumptions: The AFQMC approach relies on approximations, notably the phaseless constraint; the novelty lies in systematically exploiting the non-uniqueness of the stochastic process via gauge transformations.
figures_summary: Comparison of QMC estimators against exact FCI results demonstrating reduced bias and fluctuations when using symmetry-projected trial states (PHF+SP) versus standard methods (DHF).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the challenge, details the theoretical framework by proposing gauge augmentation (drift/Fermi gauges), discusses implementation via natural orbitals and symmetry projection, and validates these techniques on a simple shell model Hamiltonian.
why_interesting: While focused on nuclear/condensed matter Hamiltonians, the development of advanced stochastic sampling techniques applicable to fermionic dynamics is highly relevant for simulating complex quantum many-body systems in AMO physics.
